conventions.convention: The additive problem is autonomous on an open subset of R^d, with d ≥ 1; naming a component implicit does not assert existence of an implicit root.
Composition applies the rightmost map first. Lie applies a then b; Strang applies a/2, b, a/2. The bracket is [a,b] = Db·a − Da·b.
IMEX success records an unscaled update-residual check for a candidate in the selected ball; it does not independently certify forward error or a remote root.
ARS coefficients are γ = 1 − 1/√2 and δ = −1/√2. The output is Y3; stage residuals are unscaled update residuals.
The modal model uses positive mode labels k ≥ 1, eigenvalues −k², forcing gk = 1/k on odd modes and zero on even modes, and Strang composition E(h/2) B(h) E(h/2).
ARS absolute stability is a complex scalar calculation with the pole 1 − γzb = 0 excluded; it asserts no nonnormal-matrix or PDE stability.

load_bearing.statement: For d ≥ 1, c ∈ R^d, R > 0 and h > 0, suppose b is bounded by M and L-Lipschitz on the closed Euclidean ball centered at c with radius R, with hM ≤ R and hL < 1. Then Y = c + hb(Y) has exactly one root in that ball, and every candidate in that ball has distance to the root at most its unscaled residual norm divided by 1 − hL.

Under the stated uniform boundedness, Lipschitz, common compact convex tube, selected positive-radius branch-ball, exact-endpoint admission and hLb ≤ 1/2 hypotheses, the selected-root IMEX Euler map has exact-start defect at most Ch² and Lipschitz constant at most 1 + Lh, with L = 2(La + Lb).

For C³ fields under the stated compact convex tube, bounded-derivative and admitted-flow hypotheses, uniformly on K0 the Lie defect is h²[a,b]/2 + O(h³). Pointwise the Strang defect is −h³[a,[a,b]]/24 − h³[b,[a,b]]/12 + o(h³), and it is uniformly O(h³) on K0.

For each sequential implicit ARS stage, if b is bounded by M and L-Lipschitz on its selected positive-radius closed ball, with |γ|hM ≤ Rj and |γ|hL < 1, its stage equation has a unique root in that ball. Every candidate in the same ball has forward error at most its unscaled stage-residual norm divided by 1 − |γ|hL.

The diagonal maps Et form a contraction semigroup strongly continuous at zero. The domain where (Etu − u)/t has a right limit in ℓ² is exactly the set of u satisfying Σk≥1 k⁴|uk|² < ∞, and the limit is Au = (−k²uk)k≥1.

seams_checked.note: The convergence arguments preserve uniform constants, fixed positive horizon, common-tube admission, initial-error order and the separate zero-stability-constant case of the recurrence suppliers.
The explicit tableau convention is used faithfully. Coupled additive order is established directly rather than inferred from separate component orders.

ARS applies the one-stage contraction supplier with matrix [γ], preserving invariant-ball and contraction-margin hypotheses. All residual budgets retain update units and selected-branch qualifications.

This is background rather than a direct item citation. Both pages distinguish finite-matrix results from unbounded-operator claims; the diagonal heat model receives its own generator-domain proof and modal calculation.

The downstream prose explicitly declines to instantiate the batch's split maps as a coupled multirate construction. Its conditional corollary separately assumes cubic defect and stability, and does not infer them from symmetry.
The seam is conceptual: the BAOAB procedure specifies its own stochastic substeps and does not cite the deterministic Lie–Strang theorem as proof of stochastic order or invariant-measure accuracy.
